# Vienna 1683 – Scientific method & philosophical ideas

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Scientific method (conjecture, test, publish, repeat)** [`scientific_method`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_method.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Bacon, Galileo and Boyle are read. Jesuit professors show experiments but fit them into Aristotle. Nobody in Vienna publishes trials for others to repeat. Local: Jesuit college and university (mathematics and physics chairs); Wilhelm von Schröder, Fellow of the Royal Society since 1662. Elsewhere: London: Royal Society (1660); Paris: Académie des sciences (1666); Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum (1682).
- **Test claims instead of trusting authority** [`empiricism_over_authority`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/empiricism_over_authority.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Philosophy and theology are Jesuit faculties bound to Aristotle and Aquinas; medicine cites Galen and Hippocrates. Craftsmen, gunners and miners trust what works. Local: Paul de Sorbait (medical faculty); gunners and fireworkers of the arsenal. Elsewhere: London: Royal Society motto 'Nullius in verba'.
- **Controlled comparison (experiment with control group)** [`controlled_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/controlled_trial.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Van Helmont's printed challenge (1648) to divide patients by lot between two treatments is known to physicians; nobody has done it. Local: Bürgerspital; military hospitals of the garrison.
- **Placebo effect and blinded trials** [`placebo_blinding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/placebo_blinding.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Cures are credited to the remedy, the saint or the physician's standing. Hiding from a patient what he receives would look like fraud.
- **Correlation, causation and confounding** [`correlation_causation_confounding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/correlation_causation_confounding.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The comets of 1680 and 1682 are widely read as warnings of the Turkish war. 'After it, therefore because of it' is taught as a fallacy but not applied.
- **Selection and survivorship bias, fair sampling** [`selection_bias_sampling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selection_bias_sampling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Votive tablets at pilgrimage churches such as Mariazell show only those who were saved. Bacon made this point in print in 1620.
- **Measurement and quantification** [`measurement_quantification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/measurement_quantification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Surveyors, gunners, assayers and the mint measure carefully. Barometer and thermometer are known from books and court cabinets, without agreed scales. Local: Vienna mint and assay office; Daniel Suttinger (military engineer and surveyor); Georg Matthäus Vischer (map of Lower Austria, 1670). Elsewhere: London, Paris, Florence: instrument makers, barometers, thermometers.
- **Nature follows simple mathematical laws** [`mathematical_laws_of_nature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mathematical_laws_of_nature.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Kepler was imperial mathematician in Prague and Linz, yet Copernicus and Galileo's Dialogue are on the Index. Jesuits teach Tycho's system and treat mathematics as calculation. Elsewhere: Cambridge: Newton (Principia appears 1687); Paris and The Hague: Huygens; Hanover: Leibniz.
- **Falsifiability (risky, testable predictions)** [`falsifiability`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falsifiability.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Disputations are won by argument from texts. Astrology and alchemy explain every failure afterwards.
- **Fallibilism (all knowledge of nature is provisional)** [`fallibilism_provisional_knowledge`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fallibilism_provisional_knowledge.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Jesuits treat astronomical systems as hypotheses that save the appearances. Doctrine is certain; open doubt about it is dangerous.
- **Weighing evidence (base rates and Bayesian updating)** [`bayesian_reasoning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bayesian_reasoning.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Huygens' tract on games of chance (1657) and the Port-Royal Logic (1662) are in print. Nobody in Vienna works on chance. Elsewhere: Paris and the Netherlands: Pascal's heirs, Huygens; Hanover: Leibniz; Basel: Jakob Bernoulli.
- **Reproducibility and open publication** [`reproducibility_open_publication`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproducibility_open_publication.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Court alchemists sell secrets to Leopold I; Wenzel Seyler's 'transmuted' medal of 1677 was accepted. Physicians can send observations to the Miscellanea curiosa. Local: Academia Naturae Curiosorum (imperial recognition 1677), journal Miscellanea curiosa. Elsewhere: London: Philosophical Transactions (1665); Paris: Journal des sçavans (1665).
- **Systematic errors of human judgement (cognitive biases)** [`cognitive_biases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cognitive_biases.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Bacon's four idols are in print. Preachers describe self-deception as a moral fault, not as an error that can be measured.
- **Formal logic (valid deduction and fallacies)** [`formal_logic`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/formal_logic.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Aristotelian logic opens the Jesuit philosophy course; disputations in syllogisms are a public exercise. Local: University of Vienna, philosophy faculty (Jesuit since 1623).
- **Parsimony (Occam's razor)** [`occams_razor`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/occams_razor.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The maxim is taught, with Ockham as a suspect nominalist. It is not turned against angels, demons or occult qualities.
- **Thought experiment** [`thought_experiment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thought_experiment.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Scholastic cases and Galileo's falling bodies are known forms of argument.
- **Source criticism (testing documents and reports)** [`source_criticism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/source_criticism.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Peter Lambeck (died 1680) described the court library's manuscripts critically. Mabillon's method for testing charters appeared in Paris in 1681. Doubting monastery charters or saints' lives offends their owners. Local: Hofbibliothek and its manuscript commentaries by Lambeck; monastery archives (Schotten, Klosterneuburg, Melk). Elsewhere: Paris: Jean Mabillon, De re diplomatica (1681); Antwerp: Bollandists.
- **Consent and ethics of experiments on people** [`informed_consent_research_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/informed_consent_research_ethics.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Physicians try remedies on hospital poor, soldiers and prisoners without asking. Anatomies use executed criminals.
- **Natural causes (naturalism about disease, weather, comets)** [`natural_causes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_causes.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Plague and dysentery are miasma and God's punishment together; processions answer both. Comets are omens. Bayle's attack on comet fear (1682) is a Protestant book. Local: Pest-Ordnung of 1679/80 (Paul de Sorbait). Elsewhere: Rotterdam: Pierre Bayle; London: Halley observes the comet of 1682.
- **Scepticism towards astrology, omens, witchcraft and transmutation** [`scepticism_superstition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scepticism_superstition.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Leopold I patronises alchemists. Astrological calendars sell. Sorcery is a capital crime in the Ferdinandea of 1656; the Jesuit Spee's Cautio criminalis (1631) is known. Elsewhere: Salzburg: mass sorcery trials of beggar boys (from 1675); Dutch Republic: open scepticism (Balthasar Bekker, 1691).
- **Atomism (matter is made of tiny particles in motion)** [`atomism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomism.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Gassendi and Boyle are known. Jesuit teachers reject atoms because they are held to conflict with transubstantiation; Descartes has been on the Index since 1663. Elsewhere: England: Boyle's corpuscular chemistry; France: Gassendists.
- **The same physical laws on earth and in the heavens** [`universal_physical_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_physical_laws.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Schools teach a stationary earth and a separate heaven; Descartes' vortices are the known rival. Gravitation as one law is unpublished. Elsewhere: Cambridge: Newton; London: Hooke, Halley, Wren discuss the inverse-square law (1684).
- **Mechanical philosophy (explain by matter and motion, not hidden purposes)** [`mechanical_philosophy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_philosophy.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Cartesian mechanism is read privately and taught nowhere in Vienna. Substantial forms and final causes are the official physics. Elsewhere: Leiden and Utrecht: Cartesian universities; London: Boyle.
- **Idea of progress (knowledge accumulates, the future can be better)** [`idea_of_progress`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/idea_of_progress.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Cameralists promise wealth from new manufactures; Bacon's programme is known. The pulpit explains the Turk as punishment for sins, to be met with penance. Local: Wilhelm von Schröder; Philipp Wilhelm von Hörnigk.
- **Invention as a method (organised research and development)** [`systematic_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/systematic_invention.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Becher's Kunst- und Werkhaus on the Tabor (1676) was to test and teach new trades; Schröder ran it from 1677. Closed in 1681, it burns in 1683. Local: Kunst- und Werkhaus am Tabor. Elsewhere: Paris: Académie and royal manufactures (Gobelins); London: Royal Society's histories of trades.
- **Golden rule and universal ethics** [`golden_rule_universal_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/golden_rule_universal_ethics.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Preached as the Gospel rule. In practice it stops at heretics, Jews and Turks.
- **Human equality and dignity** [`human_equality_dignity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/human_equality_dignity.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Society is ranked by estate; peasants owe labour service (Robot). Equality exists before God. Turkish captives are kept as servants, and Tatars carry off Christians as slaves.
- **Natural (human) rights** [`natural_rights`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_rights.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Jurists know natural law from Suárez and Grotius; Pufendorf (1672) is a Protestant author. It binds rulers in conscience only. Locke has published nothing on it. Elsewhere: Dutch Republic and England: Grotius, Hobbes, Pufendorf in print.
- **Social contract (government by consent)** [`social_contract`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_contract.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Hobbes is read as a defence of absolute rule. Hungarian rebels under Thököly invoke the nobles' old right of resistance, abolished by Vienna in 1687.
- **Freedom of thought, speech and the press** [`freedom_of_speech_thought`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/freedom_of_speech_thought.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Every book needs approval by the Jesuit-run university censors and the bishop; Protestant books are confiscated at the gates. Elsewhere: Dutch Republic: the freest presses in Europe; England: Milton's Areopagitica (1644).
- **Religious toleration and freedom of conscience** [`religious_tolerance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/religious_tolerance.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. The Jews were expelled in 1670 and their quarter renamed Leopoldstadt. Protestants worship only in envoys' chapels (Danish, Swedish, Brandenburg, Dutch); Protestant wholesalers and Reich officials are tolerated. Local: embassy chapels; Niederlagsverwandte (privileged, partly Protestant wholesalers); Samuel Oppenheimer's household, by personal privilege. Elsewhere: Transylvania: four received religions; Dutch Republic; Brandenburg (Edict of Potsdam, 1685).
- **Secular state (separation of religious and civil authority)** [`secular_state`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secular_state.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. The dynasty's legitimacy rests on Catholic piety (Pietas Austriaca). The Counter-Reformation in the hereditary lands is state policy; the war is preached as a crusade.
- **Utilitarianism (judge rules by their consequences for everyone)** [`utilitarianism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/utilitarianism.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Cameralists argue from the 'common good' and the ruler's revenue. Morals are taught as divine law and Jesuit casuistry.
- **Abolition of judicial torture; proportionate, certain punishment** [`abolition_of_torture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_torture.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. The Ferdinandea (1656) regulates torture as the regular way to a confession in Lower Austria. Spee's objections concern witch trials only. Local: Stadtgericht and its executioner; Constitutio Criminalis Ferdinandea (1656).
- **Positive-sum cooperation (trade is not zero-sum)** [`positive_sum_cooperation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/positive_sum_cooperation.md) — K1, use wrong, make easy, accept low. Trade is seen as a contest for a fixed stock of silver: one land's gain is another's loss. Hörnigk (1684) demands buying nothing abroad that can be made at home.
- **Game theory (prisoner's dilemma, credible commitment)** [`game_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/game_theory.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Diplomats reason about commitment and betrayal case by case (Sobieski, Louis XIV, the Reich princes) without any general theory.
- **Commons problem and how communities solve it** [`tragedy_of_the_commons`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tragedy_of_the_commons.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Village customals (Banntaidinge) ration pasture, wood and water. The imperial forest office guards the Wienerwald. No general statement of the problem exists. Local: Lower Austrian Banntaidinge; Waldamt (forest office) for the Wienerwald.
